chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Burayd ibn Mu'awiya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding a man who is absent from his wife when he dies, he said: If the husband who is absent from her dies, she observes the waiting period (iddah) from the day the news reaches her, because she mourns him.

key_terms.الْغَائِبِ: The absent one (husband who is away from his wife)

ai.seo_question: When does a wife's waiting period begin if her husband dies while he is away?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's al-Istibsar clarifies the jurisprudential principle that the iddah for a missing husband begins upon the arrival of news (khabar), reflecting the Shia emphasis on practical certainty over hypothetical timelines. It underscores the legal distinction between the actual time of death and the time of notification, ensuring the wife's mourning period aligns with her awareness of the event. This ruling is foundational in fiqh al-'iddah, balancing emotional readiness with legal obligations regarding inheritance and remarriage.
